title: Bonnabelle Zabelle
text:
About Me
I am a data scientist with a background in Astrophysics research, I have been working with big data for the past 4 years. I got my B.S. in Astrophysics from the University of Minnesota in 2021. I then took a gap year working as a researcher under Prof. Claudia Scarlata. This work led me to apply to graduate school, where I ended up attending the University of Minnesota for a Masters of Science in Astrophysics, which I received at the beginning of 2025. Much of my research has been in extragalactic evolution, with an emphasis on studying star-formation rates in galaxies. Due to my affiliation with the Euclid Space Telescope I also dedicated much of my time in my masters program to working with the Euclid data pipeline, working in structure (SQL) and unstructured (DBview) databases. This work led to multiple contributions to the Euclid collaboration, mostly in the form of data validation and the creation of python-based data pipelines that enabled scientists to access Euclid data before their scheduled releases.
My education and research have led me to develop a wide array of tools well befitting that of a data scientist, from modern AI and machine learning to classics like MCMC and regression. Astrophysics has been the birthplace of many modern statistical and computational techniques, and has uniquely prepared me to embrace the ever-changing landscape of data science.

title: Bonnabelle Zabelle
text:
Experience
Graduate Research Assistant (August 2022 - January 2025)

Developed code infrastructure to allow basic users to conduct complex queries on an unstructured database.
Collaborated with a team of statisticians to create a novel Bayesian and Frequentist approach to distance measurement in Astrophysics. Served as the astrophysics reference and lead python developer.
Planned and saw through a research project at Keck Observatory, including the resulting data reduction and analysis

Bayesian Astrostatistics Teaching Assistant (2022 & 2023 Fall Semester)

Taught the foundations of Bayesian statistics through the lens of Astrophysics. Focused on modern techniques of MCMC, bayesian model selection, and hierarchical modeling.



Worked with Dr. Scarlata to create the course textbook, including testing and coding examples in R and Python.

Administrative Assistant (May 2021 - July 2022)

Administrator for the UMN Physics Force and Physics Careers, managing a range of tasks from setting up shows, career and outreach events, as well as maintaining the websites and emails.



Created a comparative report, including data acquisition and analysis, comparing the UMN undergraduate physics program to other American institutions.

Research Assistant (January 2021 - August 2022)

Ran large scale simulations of observations from the Euclid Space telescope to create a user-friendly table to quickly estimate future observations.
Lead the research and publication of a scientific paper on the role of group environments and galactic star-formation utilizing modern logistic regression techniques.
